description: SASRec predicts the next interaction using causal self-attention over a user's item history. Learned item and position embeddings pass through attention and feed-forward blocks; the resulting features score candidate items by dot product. Attention can emphasize recent interactions or draw on longer histories. Source: [Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation](https://arxiv.org/html/1808.09781).
motivation: The paper combines the simplicity of short-range sequential models with the ability to capture longer dependencies. Despite the supplied title, standard SASRec does not directly solve cold start: unseen items lack trained ID embeddings, and users with no history provide no sequential context.
implementation_notes: Start from RecHarness sasrec_perdataset and preserve all four category routes. Keep preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], and the environment's 200-epoch default. Select changes using only macro validation HR@10 under the pinned evaluator. Write artifacts beneath the trial directory. Any architecture change must update the predictor writer and DiagnosisProbe compatibility interface. The supplied description specifies a baseline and evaluation protocol, but no concrete cold-start extension or measured improvement.
pseudocode:
For each category:
  Load the unchanged benchmark split.
  Construct padded histories and shifted next-item targets.
  Encode histories with item/position embeddings and causal attention blocks.
  Train valid positions with positive and sampled-negative logistic loss.
  Select checkpoints using the permitted validation protocol.
Save category models and generate a matching routed predictor.
Report macro validation HR@10 across all four categories.

originality.positive: The original paper introduced an influential application of self-attention to sequential recommendation.
originality.negative: Using the existing SASRec baseline adds little methodological novelty; no new cold-start mechanism is specified.

future_potential.positive: Public titles and descriptions could support a content-based extension for sparse or unseen items.
future_potential.negative: That extension remains a hypothesis requiring validation within the shared search budget.

code_difficulty.positive: The existing baseline and diagnostic interface provide a straightforward starting point; score denotes difficulty on a 1–10 scale.
code_difficulty.negative: Architecture extensions require synchronized training, predictor generation, checkpoint loading, and diagnostic adapters.
